title: Nvidia opens GTC Berlin with Industrial AI Cloud push and a Merz partnership
subtitle: Jensen Huang took the keynote stage at Berlin's Tempodrom, framing Europe's first full GTC around physical AI and a sovereign German cloud run with Deutsche Telekom.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang delivered the keynote of GTC Berlin on October 21, 2026, speaking from the Tempodrom from 11:00 to 13:00 CEST on the second day of a three-day conference running October 20 to 22 at STATION Berlin. The event is Nvidia's first full-scale GTC in Europe, with more than 100 sessions spanning what the company calls the five-layer AI stack — from CUDA and accelerated computing to agentic AI, robotics, open models, and physical AI. Mercedes-Benz Group's chief technology officer is on the speaker list alongside representatives from Siemens, Audi, and Black Forest Labs.

The anchor announcement is an Industrial AI Cloud for Germany, built jointly with Deutsche Telekom. Nvidia supplies the chips — around 10,000 GPUs for the first phase — while T-Systems runs the data center on German soil, keeping customer data under German control. In a parallel announcement before the keynote, Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Huang unveiled a broader federal partnership that routes money from Germany's Hightech-Agenda fund into Telekom's cloud and a Nvidia-anchored compute buildout. Reports from Börsen-Zeitung put the public commitment in the hundreds of millions of euros.

The deal is Nvidia's largest European sovereign-AI play to date, and it fits a pattern that includes a 2025 Mistral data center in France with 18,000 Nvidia chips and the EU's $20 billion AI gigafactory initiative. The explicit goal across these deals is to reduce European dependence on U.S. hyperscalers for frontier compute. Huang used appearances in London last week to criticize Germany's slow pace on AI deployment, telling audiences that a leading industrial economy was losing its grip on the field; the Berlin partnership is the follow-through.

For learners: watch where sovereign-AI deals land the actual silicon. A cloud marketed as European or sovereign that still routes training through a U.S. data center on U.S. law isn't really sovereign — the chips, the operator, the jurisdiction, and the data residency all have to line up. That same checklist tells you whether a lab, a university, or a public-sector buyer is really free to use the system the way local policy says they can.
